messages:
Alex: quick check-in — I pushed a short note on the burst-smoothing idea. wondering if the operator should own short-term smoothing (0-60s) vs control-plane owning target-levels (5m+).
Priya: +1 we need clear boundaries. operator-local smoothing avoids cross-zone churn but can hide global oversubscription.
Mateo: operator owning short smoothing sounds right. we can keep tight SLOs by exposing a short status signal to control-plane: `local_headroom_estimate` and `stability_score`.
Lin: can you sketch the signals and how they map to admission decisions? e.g., if stability_score < 0.3 then control-plane should avoid dispatching burst lanes? 
Alex: sketch below — operator maintains a sliding window estimator and applies a leak-rate limiter for burst tokens. exports two signals every 10s: `LHE` (local_headroom_estimate), `BurstSlack` (tokens/sec).
Alex:```yaml
operator_signals:
  - name: LHE
    type: gauge
    description: estimated concurrent free slots (smoothed)
  - name: BurstSlack
    type: rate
    description: short-term tokens/sec that operator can absorb
admission_policy:
  - if LHE > 2 -> allow fastpath
  - elif BurstSlack > threshold -> allow degraded fastpath (lower token cap)
  - else -> enqueue
```
Priya: +nice. question: where do prewarm credits live? they matter for both amortization and cost accounting.
Mateo: proposal: credits are tracked in control-plane ledger (global consistency) but operator caches a soft-copy for latency. operator can spend cached credits immediately up to a window (e.g. 30s) and reconcile with ledger async.
Lin: that means operator needs a reconciliation protocol to prevent overspend and double-counting.
Alex: right — simple optimistic spend with a reconciliation delta. if ledger says negative, operator throttles and emits `overspend_event` for alerting.
Sara: ops-bot just chiming: deploy pipeline note — add a `reconcile` job to run at t+60s for cached credits. I'll create the job template.
ops-bot: created job: `operator-credit-reconcile/1729001234` -> status queued
Priya: tradeoffs: optimistic local spend reduces cold latency but can increase short-term cost. we should bound operator cache to a percent of tenant commit (e.g., max 5%).
Mateo: also need experiment plan A/B: A = operator-cached credits on, B = cached credits off; measure 95p latency and short-term cost variance.
Alex: agreed. metrics to add: `inflight_token_ratio`, `kvcache_hit_rate`, `reconcile_conflicts_per_min`, `operator_local_spend`.
Lin: about scaling down: we should extend drain window if operator reports high `stability_score` drop during drain, otherwise aggressive drains are fine for cost.
Priya: good call. add one more signal: `drain_friction` (0-1) computed from inflight_job_count and tail-latency.
Sara: I'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to lock boundary decisions and owners.
Alex: action items I note: 1) Mateo to write operator proto for LHE/BurstSlack (PR by EOD), 2) Priya to update cost bounds doc (max cached credit %), 3) Lin to prototype reconcile backoff and conflict handling, 4) Sara to add reconcile job + schedule sync.
Mateo: starting the proto now. ping if you want a quick walkthrough.
Lin: i'll prototype exponential backoff for reconcile and a fast-path delta rollback.
Priya: can we add a really small smoke test for overspend behavior in our sim harness? catches regressions early.
Alex: yes — sim harness test + canary with 1 tenant first. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
thread_text: quick check-in on operator vs control-plane boundaries for burst smoothing
